newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes expects to achieve yr gold target.
newsitem.headline: Macraes expects to achieve yr gold target.

text.p: Macraes Mining Company Ltd said on Thursday it expected gold production in the current half to be slightly lower than in the first half, but still expected to achieve a full year budget production of 130,000 ounces.
Macraes made the forecast after reporting a first half net profit of NZ$7.05 million, up 421 percent on the $1.35 million profit in the previous comparable period.
"The sharp improvement....was a direct result of higher gold production and rising efficiencies at the company's gold project near Dunedin in New Zealand," Macraes said in a statement.
"Total gold output in the current half is forecast to be down slightly on the opening six month period as the project treats lower grade material, especially during the third quarter."
Third quarter gold production was expected to be approximately 27,000 ounces.
Steady progress was being made on the company's plans to substantially expend the Macraes project.
In July, the company announced that it would lift production rate to nine million tonnes of ore a year with the construction of a new NZ$120 million processing plant.
After the expansion, gold production from the two operating plants at the mine would rise from its current level of around 130,000 ounces a year to between 320,000 ounces and 350,000 ounces a year.
"This will make Macraes project one of the top five gold producers in the Australasian region," Macraes said.
Exploration expenditure, mainly at the Macraes minesite, was up 57 percent to NZ$5.9 million in the June half.
